long_biography.plain_text:
Douglas Alexander “Sandy” Warner III joined Morgan Guaranty after graduating from Yale and rose through posts in New York and London to lead J.P. Morgan. As chairman and chief executive, he helped drive the bank’s shift toward investment banking and guided its combination with Chase. He completed the merged group’s integration before retiring after a 33-year career.

Beyond banking, Warner became a long-serving institutional governor. He chaired Memorial Sloan Kettering for 20 years and co-led major capital campaigns that supported research and clinical expansion. He also served on Yale’s governing board and investment committee, bringing his banking and governance experience to the university’s endowment stewardship. He later became an honorary chair at Memorial Sloan Kettering.
